When I visited Ukraine at the chance, to talk to Crimean victims of the Russian occupation, and their tales were horrifying. I met a young boy who was forced to join the Russian Navy, and in the training camp he had dared to put down the Russian flag and replace it by his underwear. And I stood speechless at the bravery of that young boy. And that's why I'm proud to be here today, not only to confirm our principled position, that Crimea is an inalienable part of Ukraine under the international law, but also to confirm our respect and support to all citizens in the peninsula who courageously stand up for their opinions and for their fights for those of their community. Slava Ukraini.
Thank you, Prime Minister. And I am very pleased to invite His Excellency John Antonio Briseno, Prime Minister of Belize.

Thank you very much, Excellency President Zelensky. Belize recognize your bravery and stands by you and your people. I wish to reaffirm Belize's firm commitment to Ukraine and that Crimea must be allowed to be where it rightfully belongs with Ukraine. We attach high regard to the rule of law and to the peaceful settlement of disputes. As testament to this conviction, my country together with Guatemala has submitted our territorial dispute to the International Court of Justice for a final peaceful and just resolution. In an international climate where multilateralism has been made fragile, it is important that small states support one another to ensure foundational principles and values are upheld. Belize has participated in the Crimea Platform before as a symbol of solidarity. Belize values every country with which it has established bilateral relations. Belize is also pleased to announce that we support the New York Declaration. Belize and Ukraine's bilateral relationship should work to advance new avenues intertwining diplomatic support with trade and people-to-people cultural ties. May God continue to bless the people of Ukraine. Thank you so much.
Thank you, Mr. Prime Minister. And I kindly invite His Excellency, Prime Minister of the Republic of Bulgaria, Rosen Zhelyazkov, to deliver his address.

Thank you. Dear President Zelensky, Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, As absurd as it may seem, we are now into the fourth year of Russia's unfair, unlawful, unjust, and provocative war of aggression against Ukraine. Russia's full-scale invasion began February 22, but the aggression started 11 years earlier with the illegal occupation of Crimea, the event that triggered a wave of military escalation that continues to this day. The annexation of Crimea constitutes a brutal violation of international law, including the UN Charter. Sovereign states will have a duty to condemn and reject actions that undermine the principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity. Bulgaria's commitment to the non-recognition of Russia's illegal annexation of Crimea, Sevastopol, and part of Donetsk, Kherson, Lugansk, and Zaporozhye remains firm. This Regions are and will remain part of Ukraine. Honourable colleagues, we strongly condemn the forced displacement and deportation of Ukrainian children to the Russian Federation, where they are subject to re-education and stripped of their identity. We call for full access for international human rights monitors to occupied areas. Accountability for all violations must be ensured. Crimea was once a sunny resort on the Black Sea, but the Russian occupation has turned into a launchpad for missile and drone attacks in southern Ukraine, effectively a battleground. We want to see Crimea as a place for recreation, not war. We urge the Russian Federation to commit to the diplomatic process led by the President of the United States, But sadly, Russia will still believe in bloodshed, not peace. A peace deal must not result in a frozen conflict or territorial concessions, which would embolden future aggression. It must include credible security guarantees for Ukraine and consider the interests of both Ukraine and Europe. Thank you.

Thank you, Mr. Prime Minister. And it is my honor to invite His Excellency Prime Minister of Cabo Verde, Mr. Ulisses Correia e Silva to take the floor. We are truly delighted to have you with us today.

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Thank you, President Zelenskyy, for inviting us for this important platform. President Zelenskyy, we consider this meeting important as we see it as a way to find more sustainable and lasting solution to the war in your country, Ukraine. The government of Cabo Verde, since February 2022, had a firm position regarding this conflict. We didn't change our position. We maintain our position on the right side of history. Cabo Verde is a country that respects international law, international law for all. for all, for all. We maintain that respect for territorial integrity is a fundamental principle and sine qua non condition for peaceful relations between countries, between states, and therefore for international peace and security. Dialogue, peaceful settlement, and of conflicts and cooperation must prevail. International law, international rules based art shall not undermine as the international community is striving to ensure a peaceful world.

I thank you for your kind attention.
God bless Ukraine. Thank you, Mr. Prime Minister. Our next speaker is Taoiseach of Ireland, His Excellency, Mr. Micheal Martin.

Thank you, President Zelensky, Excellencies, and friends. It's over three years since the launch of Russia's full-scale, unprovoked, and unjustified war of aggression against Ukraine. It's 11 years since this aggression began in Crimea with Russia's illegal annexation. Russia could and should end its brutal war at this moment. All it has to do is halt its attacks, accept an unconditional ceasefire, and come to the negotiating table. But it chooses not to do so and instead intensifies its air attacks against Ukraine's towns and cities, deliberately targeting civilians and essential infrastructure. These are not the actions of a country seeking peace. Mr. President, you and the people of Ukraine have Ireland's full support as you stand against this brutal Russian aggression. We cannot allow force to be the means by which international borders are defined. We cannot return to a world where we accept that might is right. I hope that we have learned the painful lessons of history not to allow this to happen. The international community must stand firm in our refusal to recognize the legitimacy of Russia's actions. When a state transgresses international law, as we have seen with Russia's annexation of Crimea and its illegal full-scale war against Ukraine, it threatens not only the immediate victims and those on the front line, but also unravels the fabric that binds our global community. Ukraine is a sovereign, independent nation and a full member of these United Nations. Like each one of us here, it must be afforded the fundamental right to peace and security and full respect for its internationally recognized borders. Justice is not just a matter of principle, but rather it forms the very foundations from which we must build a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace for Ukraine. Any peace agreement must uphold Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity based on respect for the principles of the UN Charter and for international law. And this includes continued recognition that Russia's violation of these principles in Ukraine began not in 2022, but in 2014. I'm deeply concerned about the reports of human rights abuses abuses in Russian-occupied Crimea and in all the Ukrainian territories illegally held by Russia. Russian efforts to change the demographic composition of the peninsula, its attack on the Ukrainian language, culture and identity, and its callous suppression of the Crimean Tatar community must be strongly condemned. Ireland welcomes and supports the New York Declaration, and I use this opportunity again to reiterate Ireland's firm condemnation of the Russian Federation's continued aggression against Ukraine. We salute you, President Zelenskyy, and your government for your leadership, resilience, and courage. It continues to inspire. Ireland and the European Union will always stand with the Ukrainian people for as long as it takes. Slava Ukraini.
Thanks a lot, Your Excellency. It's my honor to give the floor to His Excellency, Mr. Luc Frieden, Prime Minister of Luxembourg.

Mr. President, dear Volodymyr, dear friends, 11 years of Crimea's occupation by Russia, 11 years of oppression, of systemic human rights violations and suffering. We, the international community, must resolutely continue to reject this act of blatant aggression. This is, and this remains, a direct assault on the principles that keep our world together: sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the inviolability of borders. That is why this platform matters. It gives us unity, it gives us a voice, it keeps Russia accountable. Luxembourg is proud to support this work. And we know what is at stake. As a country invited twice in the last century, we will never accept a world where force dictates law. It was here in America that one of my predecessors, Prime Minister in exile, asked for the support of the U.S. and international community to give us back our independence. We succeeded only because We were not alone. And today, this room shows you, Mr. President Volodymyr, that you do not stand alone in this fight. Since 2014, the United Nations General Assembly has spoken with clarity and conviction. The charter must be upheld. Respect for the UN charter is not a matter of choice. It is a very foundation of peace, prosperity, and security. Russia's action show contempt for international law and humanitarian principles. Borders cannot and must not be redrawn by force. And therefore, let me once again pay tribute to Ukrainian people. Your courage, your resilience, your determination. You are not only defending your land, you are defending the values we share. You continue to inspire us. Luxembourg stands firmly with Ukraine. Your fight for freedom is our fight too. And we will remain by your side until peace, full sovereignty and justice prevails. Thank you.
Thank you, Mr. Prime Minister. Our next speaker is the Prime Minister of the Republic of Malta, His Excellency Mr. Robert Abela. Please.

President Zelensky, dear Volodymyr, Excellencies, Friends, Crimea is Ukraine. Eleven years since its forced annexation, the Russian Federation continues to assert its illegitimate occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol in violation of Article 2, sub-article 4 of the UN Charter. Together with our international partners, present in today's summit, and I thank you for that, Malta and the EU will continue to affirm our unwavering support for the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. The restoration of the territorial integrity of Ukraine will be a crucial step for the restoration of a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace for Ukraine. the face of Russia's unjustified presence inside the Crimean Peninsula, Malta maintains its unwavering support for the Ukrainian residents enduring occupation by Russian de facto authorities. We take this occasion to condemn Russia's attempts to change, or even worse, erase Ukraine's national identity and way of life via the forced imposition of Russian citizenship. By applying military suppression and intimidation, the Russian Federation is aiming to permanently alter the Crimean peninsula's demographic structures, further to those in Ukraine's other Russian-occupied territories. Mr. President, as we speak, Russian occupying authorities inside Crimea continue to impose harsh bans on the Ukrainian language, traditions, as well as holidays to this day. Sadly, we understand that such restrictive measures are ultimately paving the way towards a militarized policy of Russification, one which ultimately erases the indigenous and folkloric voices of the Ukrainian people inside this region. Regretfully, this complements the Russian Federation's unlawful deportation, as well as the forced transfer of Ukrainian children from Crimea, resulting in changes to the identity and citizenship of Ukrainian children. In Malta's current role as President of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe, we have and will continue to place specific attention on children impacted by Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and will continue to advocate for the immediate return of forcibly displaced Ukrainian children to their respective homelands, including Crimea. To conclude, We believe that Russia's actions mark a stark violation of the principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independence of states, as boldly enshrined in the UN charter. In adopting the summit's New York declaration, we therefore reaffirm that the right for reintegration of the Crimean peninsula as part of Ukraine is non-negotiable. Without any further delay, Malta calls on the Russian Federation to immediately reverse its illegal occupation of Crimea together with the other four Russian annexed territories. Slava Ukraine. Thank you.
Thank you, Mr. Prime Minister. And I am very pleased to invite His Excellency Mr. Yasar Guler, Minister of National Defense of the Republic of Turkey. Buyrun.

Thank you. Esteemed President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky, Honorable National Leader of the Crimean Tatars and Members of the Ukrainian Parliament, Mr. Mustafa Krimovolo, distinguished heads of states and government, dear Crimean Tatar brothers and sisters, it is an honor to be with you today at this summit on the 18th anniversary of the United Nations, once again highlighting the Crimean cause. For us, the peaceful resolution of Crimea is not inseparable from the quest for a just and lasting peace in Ukraine. The Crimean Tatars have long been an integral part of Ukraine's diverse fabric and they contributed to peace and stability. Turkey has never recognized the illegal annexation of Crimea And we have stood firm since 2014 supporting Ukraine's independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, including Crimea. Defending the rights of the Crimean Tatars is not only a matter of foreign policy, but a historical and moral duty for us. We will continue our relentless pursuit to amplify their voices, protect their rights, and ensure their freedom and dignity. It is encouraging to see Ukraine safeguarding the rights of our Tatar brothers and sisters. We will continue to support President Zelensky's commitment to the Crimean cause. Turkey will continue its efforts towards this end. In closing, I would like to reaffirm Turkey's commitment to the Crimean platform and express our hope to advance not only the Crimean cause, but also the enduring interests of independent, prosperous, and sovereign Ukraine. Thank you.

Thank you, Mr. Minister. Dear excellencies, dear colleagues, allow me at this moment to thank His Excellency President Zelensky for his participation in the fifth Crimean Platform. Dear colleagues, I am very pleased to invite her excellency, Ms. Elina Valtanen, Chairperson in Office of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, Minister of Finland.

Thank you, Chair, Excellencies. I have the privilege to speak today both as the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Finland and as the Chairperson in Office of the OSCE, the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe. The OSCE core principles and commitments stemming from the Helsinki Final Act mirror the central tenets of the UN Charter. They include the respect for sovereign equality, territorial integrity, the inviolability of borders, the non-intervention in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. These principles remain as vital as ever, despite Russia's war of aggression that blatantly violates them. Justice is a key component of sustainable peace. The OSCE contributed significantly to documenting Russia's violations of international law, with a focus on deported Ukrainian children, arbitrarily detained civilians and prisoners of war. I am acutely concerned about the dire human rights situation of Crimean Tatars and Ukrainians living on Crimean Peninsula. It has been more than 11 years since the Russian occupation began. Today, we reiterate that Crimea is Ukraine, and the city of Sevastopol is Ukraine. The territorial integrity of Ukraine must be restored. There is no place for imperialism in the 21st century. We remain committed to the UN Charter and the Helsinki principles and unwavering in our support to Ukraine and its people. Glory to Ukraine.
Thank you, Madam Minister. Now I am honored to invite His Excellency, Mr. Takeshi Iwaya, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan, who will deliver the message on behalf of the Prime Minister of Japan.

Thank you, Minister Shivah. Today, I'd like to deliver the statement of Prime Minister of Japan, Mr. Ishiba, on his behalf. Three and a half years have passed since the beginning of Russia's aggression against Ukraine. We renew our respect for the day-to-day effort of the Ukrainian people to defend their country and freedom. The host of this meeting, President Zelenskyy, encourages Ukrainian people every day and night who endure tension and anxiety and fight for their own future, a president bravely makes every single effort toward peace and homeland. We would like to express our utmost respect for him. Japan supports the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine, including Crimea. We are deeply concerned about the suffering of those who were displaced from their home, including Crimea. Through today's meeting, we reaffirm to the international community the principle that unilateral change of the status quo by force is unacceptable. Russia continues its brutal attacks, showing no signs of concrete steps toward peace. Now is the time for us to stand united together to draw a swift and positive response from Russia that leads to a just and lasting peace. We welcome President Trump's strong leadership and his tireless diplomatic effort in pursuit of this vital goal. The intensive discussions on security guarantees for Ukraine, mainly led by European countries, are very important for achieving peace. Japan is determined to actively participate in these discussions and to play an appropriate role in bringing peace to Ukraine. From this viewpoint, Japan is in coordination with the international community to support Ukraine and to put sanctions against Russia. On September the 12th, we announced additional sanctions against Russia. We will continue our unwavering support for Ukraine and promote our effort for recovery and reconstruction through public-private partnership to strengthen social and economic resilience of Ukraine, to move closer to achieving two goals, which are an early ceasefire and a just and lasting peace, Japan will closely work with all countries present today. Thank you.
Thank you, Your Excellency, and I am very pleased to invite the last speaker, Her Excellency Minister, Ms. Maria Malmer Stenengard.

Dear Ukrainian friends, friends of Ukraine, allow me to briefly make two points. First, Russia is the aggressor and aggression must never be rewarded. Crimea is Ukraine, as are Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia. Respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity is not optional. Disregarding the rules and principles enshrined in the UN Charter would not only risk renewed aggression against Ukraine, but would also set a dangerous precedent. Moreover, we owe this to the Ukrainians on the temporarily occupied areas and to those who bravely fight for their freedom. Second, justice will prevail. We are firmly committed to ensuring full accountability for the countless crimes and human rights violations. Eleven years after the illegal annexation of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol, and almost four years into the full scale invasion, independent reports have documented large scale violations of international law. These include extrajudicial killings, arbitrary arrests, torture, unlawful deportations and forcible transfer of children, forced mobilization of Ukrainian civilians into Russia's armed forces, politically motivated prosecutions, and repression of ethnic and religious groups, in particular Crimean Tatars. Accountability is key for justice to the victims and a deterrent against future violations. In this context, we welcome the steps taken towards establishing a special tribunal for the crime of aggression against Ukraine. Before ending, I would like to underline that since Russia shows no interest in peace, as shown by the continuous attacks on civilians, we must keep maximizing our pressure on Russia and support for Ukraine in its legitimate pursuit of a just and lasting peace.

Thank you, Madam Minister. Dear friends, dear colleagues, ladies and gentlemen, excellencies, dear friends, as we close this summit, I thank all those who joined us today despite the demanding schedule of this week. This format was created by President Zelensky in 2021, yet it has proven to be as relevant as ever. Every year, the number of its participants keeps growing. This means that the issue of Crimea and the principle of territorial integrity remains critical for national all over the world. On behalf of Ukraine, I thank every nation that stands with us, every nation that shares the ultimate goal of restoring a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace grounded in the charter of the United Nations. For Ukraine, as a founding member of the UN, the charter is not simply a document. It is the cornerstone of the international law. Restoring Ukraine's territorial integrity is essential to restoring the authority of the charter. International law shall prevail. Peace must be restored and secured. And this is only possible through strength. I now officially declare the fifth summit of the International Crimea Platform closed. Our work must go further. Today, the entire international order can be expressed in three words. Crimea is Ukraine. These words make a difference. And most importantly, as I said in the beginning, this summit sends a signal of hope to Ukrainians and Crimean Tatars in Crimea. The world did not forget. Ukraine did not forget. And we will never abandon you and our goal of restoring justice. I thank everyone present for standing with Ukraine and international law. Thank you for your attention.
